A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices A–J are readable and support comparison after matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v1 reports original transformer-training experiments on OpenWebText and FineWeb, including hyperparameter sweeps, optimizer comparisons, and compute-optimal scaling analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and reports additional optimizer-scaling and spectral-normalization results.

M1.justification: The proposed scaling prescriptions in Tables 1–2 and the optimizer components remain unchanged. Appendix A corrects SOAP’s moment projection and grafting’s norm notation to agree with methods already described in v1; this does not establish a changed implemented procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate language modeling on OpenWebText and FineWeb. Larger SOAP models and normalization comparisons retain those tasks and datasets. The new discussion of C4 does not report an evaluation on it.

E2.justification: New Figure 14 explicitly compares spectrally normalized counterparts against µP-scaled SOAP, Muon, and Shampoo in the Llama scaling experiment. SOAP itself was already evaluated in v1’s appendix, including Figures 11–12.

E3.justification: SOAP’s reported scaling experiment extends to the 1.4B model; v1’s Figure 12 stopped at 640M for SOAP. Section H.6 adds matched normalization comparisons and hyperparameter perturbations under the retained Section 4 setup. Datasets, token budgets, architectures, and compute-multiplier definition otherwise remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Section H.6 and Figures 14–15 add a focused investigation of whether spectral normalization helps large-model scaling, including learning-rate, weight-decay, and warmup perturbations for normalized variants. Earlier blocking, depth-transfer, finite-width, and tokens-per-parameter analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report the same estimated 0.1% loss noise floor from nondeterminism in Section H.3. No new seed counts, repeated-run reporting, confidence intervals, or significance-testing procedures are introduced.

E6.justification: Figures 1, 6, and 12 add or revise SOAP scaling results, including its 1.4B result. Figures 14–15 newly show no advantage from spectral normalization in this setting and worse scaling for normalized Shampoo. These variant comparisons do not establish a same-setting improvement over v1. The 9.6 and 7.4 optimal tokens-per-parameter estimates and Table 5 values are unchanged.

T1.justification: Sections B.4–B.5 add direct Newton–Schulz and AdaMuon scaling derivations, while Appendix C expands optimizer-specific depth arguments. Section B.10 revises the Gram-matrix assumptions and eigenvalue reasoning, and Appendix A repairs update formulas. These strengthen localized mathematical support for the existing scaling rules.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and discussion extend the headline claim of consistent speedups across 190M–1.4B models to SOAP. v1 highlighted Muon at 1.4× and Shampoo at 1.3×; v2 summarizes all three as near 1.4×. The central claim that reliable optimizer comparisons require good hyperparameter transfer is retained.

C2.justification: Section H.5 adds hypotheses linking the low optimal token count to FineWeb’s quality and extensive tuning. Section H.6 explains the lack of normalization gains through blocking and attributes Shampoo’s deterioration to tuning near instability and shifting optima. Appendix J’s stated limitations remain substantively unchanged.

D1.justification: Section D.3 newly specifies Shampoo’s exponents as eL = eR = 1/2, clarifying the existing experiment. Section H.6 explains which layers normalization affects in hybrid Muon. Hardware descriptions, Table 4 tuning values, and code and experiment-log access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations to Dion and Scion, credits earlier identification of Muon’s learning-rate scaling, and discusses Scion’s hyperparameter transfer. This modestly refines prior-work positioning. The updated bibliographic entry for Scaling Collapse represents the same cited work.

P1.justification: v2 corrects grammar and terminology, removes duplicated initialization prose, and expands several appendix explanations through localized subsections. The main narrative and overall appendix organization remain intact.

P2.justification: Figures 1 and 6 are redrawn to include SOAP, Figure 12 is revised, and Figures 14–15 are added. Some tables and figures are reformatted or relocated. Figure 12 loses its scaling-rule legend, reducing interpretability; most existing graphical displays remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: The added derivations and corrected update formulas make the scaling prescriptions easier to audit. The new normalization controls provide useful evidence about their applicability and failure conditions. These are limited overall gains, tempered by Figure 12’s missing legend and ambiguity between H.1’s normalized-SOAP description and the variants distinguished in H.6.
